ai_summary: Great Britain is currently generating 3.2 GW of wind power, with estimated Scottish wind output contributing 2.1 GW, representing 20.8% of Scotland's installed wind capacity. While this abundant renewable generation drives Scottish carbon intensity down to 0 gCO2/kWh, the wider GB-wide grid remains reliant on fossil fuels, operating at 219 gCO2/kWh. Critical north-south transmission bottlenecks prevent this clean electricity from reaching demand centres, forcing grid operators to instruct Scottish wind farms to reduce generation. Consequently, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 849 MWh, accumulating a constraint cost of about £47,969. To compensate for this stranded green energy, an estimated 161,329 m3 of gas has been burned elsewhere on the network, needlessly emitting 297 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere. Annualising today's expenditure yields an estimated total yearly curtailment cost of approximately £18 million. Recovered through system balancing charges across national electricity demand, this recurring inefficiency represents an estimated increase of roughly £0.06/MWh on everybody's invoice in the UK, highlighting the ongoing financial and carbon costs of transmission grid constraints.
